label: prop:a-8-partition-function-identity
title: $a_8$ partition-function identity: $a_8(X) = \sum_{n=1}^{5} p(n)\,X^{5-n}$
html:
Let a_8 \in \mathbb{Z}[X] denote the top-shared (m = 8) integer Habiro coefficient of the proton and neutron in the canonical Habiro-witness convention:

  a_8(X) \;=\; X^4 + 2\,X^3 + 3\,X^2 + 5\,X + 7.

Then a_8 admits the closed form

  a_8(X) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^{5} p(n)\,X^{5-n},

where p(n) denotes the integer partition function (Hardy–Ramanujan, OEIS A000041): p(1) = 1,\; p(2) = 2,\; p(3) = 3,\; p(4) = 5,\; p(5) = 7.

Categorical interpretation

The integer partition function p(n) appears throughout Habiro-ring / Hecke representation theory:

  • Number of Young diagrams of weight n (equivalently: partitions of n).
  • Generating function \sum_{n \geq 0} p(n)\,q^n = \prod_{k \geq 1} (1 - q^k)^{-1} = 1 / (q;q)_\infty — the Euler / Habiro generating series.
  • Dimensions of basis elements indexed by Young diagrams via the Robinson–Schensted correspondence (combined with \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim(\lambda)^2 = n!).

The appearance of p(1), p(2), p(3), p(4), p(5) as successive coefficients of a_8(X) strongly suggests that the m = 8 shell of the Habiro tower is counting partitions of n = 1, \dots, 5 — i.e., a_8(X) is the dimension-generating function of partitions fitting within the m = 8 shell.

Convention stability

This identification was made in the Habiro-witness convention (include_inter=True). The partition-function structure is much more convention-robust than the cyclotomic prefactors: it is a property of the combinatorial counting at the m = 8 shell, not of the algebraic-expansion shape, so this finding is expected to survive a change of convention.

The Hardy–Ramanujan values (1, 2, 3, 5, 7) are standard (OEIS A000041 Table 1; Andrews, The Theory of Partitions, §1.1).

Cross-references

  • Sibling Lean identity (cyclotomic strand-doubling): cyclotomic-strand-doubling.md
  • categorical source: the canonical formalism

The coincidence recorded here is a categorical Habiro-shell observation rather than a new deductive argument.
